cells.cell: JCS function against vectors-a2a-jcs-v01 (rfc8785 target)
cells.detail: AER-1 does not claim RFC 8785: draft -26 Section 12 says it carries the producer's exact bytes 'rather than mandating a canonicalization scheme such as ... RFC8785'. Its own serialization (Sections 3.1 and 7.1: code point key order, ensure_ascii escapes) was run through the contract anyway as a measurement: 34 of 53 vectors match RFC 8785, 19 differ (non-ASCII escaped as \u, UTF-16 versus code point key order, lone surrogates accepted, 1e-06 style numbers). The serializer is written from the draft text, not the kit's code, so this is a measurement, not a failed claim.

cells.cell: single-receipt vectors (21 valid, 36 invalid, 1 profile-invalid) recomputed from draft -26 Section 6
cells.detail: 48 of 58 with draft-zambo-aer1-26 read verbatim (the latest revision; -27 is 404). Differs: 10 valid vectors (bound-04, deep-nesting, edge-numbers, empty-members, input-hash-multikey-20, large-payload, maximum-offset-timestamp, optional-members-18, typographic-unicode, uuid-v1-core). Each declares receipt_schema_version "0.4", carries no metadata_hash, and sits in the kit's valid/ set, where every file MUST conform. Draft reading: Table 1 makes metadata_hash 'REQUIRED when receipt_schema_version is "0.4" or later', and Section 6 step 4 says 'A "0.4" receipt without metadata_hash MUST fail.' So all ten are rejected. Kit reading, from its runner: 'Absence of metadata_hash is not failed'. So all ten are accepted, and the kit's own runner returns accept on these bytes. The draft's conformance bar (Implementation Status; Section 11 SHOULD) is byte-identical verdicts to the runners, so the draft's procedure and its conformance bar disagree on exactly these ten. Controls: adding a correct metadata_hash flips our verdict on 10 of 10 (the kit accepts the same digests); removing it from valid/real-04 flips ours to reject, while the kit still accepts it, even after created_at is moved one minute. With the kit's rule, 57 of 58 agree, and the remaining one is invalid/lowercase-timestamp.json: the kit rejects lower-case t and z, but RFC 3339 section 5.6 allows them and -26 adds no case rule. Under the verbatim reading that vector agrees on outcome only, because it also lacks metadata_hash.
cells.evidence: adapters/aer1-run.txt and adapters/aer1-kit-reading-run.txt (adapters/aer1_adapter.py); review with the kit's own runner, tampers and controls: adapters/aer1-review-run.txt (adapters/aer1_review.py)

cells.cell: chain commitments, Section 7.3 (8 vectors)
cells.detail: 7 of 8 against draft-zambo-aer1-26 (the latest revision; -27 is 404). Differs: x-entry-count-float, whose entry_count is written 5.0 over a 5-entry chain. Kit reading: it expects invalid, and its runner says 'commitment entry_count is not an integer'. That is Python isinstance(int); the JavaScript runner regex-rewrites the file to mirror that check. Draft reading: Section 7.3 defines entry_count as 'a JSON number with an integer value', so 5.0 is valid. Section 7.1 uses the same phrase for seq and adds 'The representations 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; both are accepted'. No sentence in -26 restricts how entry_count is spelled. RFC 8259 section 6 allows a fraction part and has no separate integer type. The kit itself expects valid for v07-seq-float-valid (seq 1.0, 2.0). Controls: spelling 5.0 as 5 flips the kit's runner to valid, and the case agrees. Spelling commit-valid-1's 5 as 5.0 flips the kit's runner to invalid, while ours stays valid.
